answer: Every submission must name 2 parent transactions it builds on, and an orphan with no accepted parent earns no weight. The onyx graph is validated at intake and the grove frontier is published, thus the ancestry of every answer is public, and spiral anchors the chain at a checkpoint. A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 136 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
